definitions.explanation: A person who travels from place to place selling goods, rather than operating from a fixed shop. Historically common in Japan before the modern retail era.

examples.japanese: {行商人|ぎょうしょうにん}が{村|むら}にやってきた。
examples.english: A peddler came to the village.

examples.japanese: {昔|むかし}はこの{道|みち}を{行商人|ぎょうしょうにん}が{行|い}き{来|き}していた。
examples.english: In the old days, peddlers used to come and go along this road.

examples.japanese: {祖父|そふ}は{若|わか}いころ{行商人|ぎょうしょうにん}として{全国|ぜんこく}を{回|まわ}り、{魚|さかな}や{野菜|やさい}を{売|う}り{歩|ある}いていた。
examples.english: When my grandfather was young, he traveled the country as a peddler, selling fish and vegetables.

notes:
A compound of {行商|ぎょうしょう} (peddling, itinerant trade) and {人|にん} (person). The base word {行商|ぎょうしょう} can also be used on its own to refer to the activity of peddling.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {行商|ぎょうしょう}をする (to peddle)
- {行商|ぎょうしょう}に{出|で}る (to go out peddling)
- {行商人|ぎょうしょうにん}として{働|はたら}く (to work as a peddler)

Historically, {行商人|ぎょうしょうにん} played an important role in distributing goods to rural areas. Today the term appears mainly in historical contexts. Modern equivalents include {移動販売|いどうはんばい} (mobile sales) for food trucks and similar businesses.
